title: Reconsider representation before introducing self-referential unsafe machinery
task: Review a graph-like Rust structure that proposes raw internal pointers plus Pin because borrowed self-references are difficult to express.
context: One container clearly owns all nodes.
Edges only need stable handles to nodes, not direct references.
Node deletion is infrequent and can update derived indexes.
evidence: The raw-pointer design would add unsafe code and pinning invariants.
Reference-counted nodes would add allocation/reference-counting overhead.
An arena/vector plus typed index handles can represent the same graph.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Use raw pointers because the borrow checker is getting in the way.
Wrap every node in Arc to make lifetimes disappear.
Treat Pin as the default solution for any self-reference.
expected_decision_properties: Reconsider the data representation before adding unsafe/lifetime machinery.
Compare typed index/arena handles against raw pointers and reference counting.
Account for deletion/index-update cost rather than pretending index handles are free.
Prefer the lowest-total-complexity representation for the actual mutation pattern.
unacceptable_reasoning: Borrow-checker difficulty proves unsafe is necessary.
Arc is free enough to use without lifecycle/performance analysis.
Direct references are always more idiomatic than stable indexes.
expected_tradeoffs: index indirection/update bookkeeping vs lifetime/unsafe complexity
reference counting overhead vs explicit ownership
verification_expectations: Test deletion/movement semantics for index validity.
Benchmark only if the extra indirection is performance-sensitive.
If unsafe remains, document and tool-check its invariants.
notes: Grounded in Rust for Rustaceans Chapter 13 index-pointer pattern and earlier ownership/unsafe chapters.
